source_title: Los Angeles Daily News, 1990-10-07, "The sheriff's shootings: minorities are a majority" (David Parrish and Beth Barrett), p. N1; NewsBank docref news/0EF60E8A54B29943; companion story news/0EF60E8A713DDF97
quote: In those 146 other cases, 34 percent - 49 people - were fatal shootings.
note: The Daily News reviewed all 202 on-duty, deputy-involved shootings (people hit) from Jan 1, 1985 to Jul 27, 1990. 26 of the 56 cases it questioned were fatal, as were 49 of the other 146: 75 deaths. No yearly breakdown is given. Entered as a period total with its exposure (protocol deviation approved by JN 2026-11-15), because the LA Times is not in NewsBank and the Daily News recall in a later window was about 29%. The 1991-94 years come from Special Counsel Bobb's reports. Amnesty International (AMR 51/76/92) gives 26 'fatally shot' in 1990, but that appears to misattribute the Daily News 26-of-56 figure (its LAPD 1990 figure, 18, also conflicts with LAPD's 39), so it is not used.

source_title: The Sun (Baltimore, MD), Sep 10 - Dec 31, 1990 (case-by-case reconstruction; no deaths found)
note: The Sun enters NewsBank on Sep 10, 1990, and no other paper covers Baltimore County before then, so 1990 is a partial year (exposure about 0.31). With 1991-94 this gives about 4.3 exposure-years, short of the 5-year minimum, so the agency stays out of the main comparison (JN decision 2026-11-22).
